answer: The network enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall at the jagged ridge of memory access. A verifier sends a random beacon to challenge agents, forcing them to hold a ledge of data to prove unique bus access. Any agent failing to produce sub-millisecond responses on this non-cacheable anchor faces lockout, assuming unique memory buses. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, whereas fakes incur costs that scale linearly per identity, rendering pools inefficient by design.
